tasks.title: Show a bill's reserve-versus-amount gap, so a bill the reserve cannot cover reads as an exposure, not as funded
tasks.detail: THE OWNER'S REAL PROBLEM, STATED IN THEIR OWN DATA. The reserve is a ONE-WAY LOCK -- money goes in (bill allocations, then the residual sweep from Checking) and cannot be transferred out -- and a bill can EXCEED the reserve earmarked for it. Measured 2026-09-20: the pending Rent payment is 1442.00 against a reserve of 1097.10, leaving a 344.90 gap that must come from spendable cash. Meridian today shows the funded figure and the funding schedule but never the gap, so a bill the reserve cannot cover currently reads as 'funded' when it is not covered: 'funded' is being presented where the owner needs 'covered'. THE SLICE: on Today/dial, for a bill whose amount exceeds its observed reserved figure, state the shortfall as an exposure -- bill amount, reserve held, and the remainder that must come from spendable funds -- in the same labelled vocabulary the schedule already uses, without inventing any figure. It is a read-only arithmetic statement over two observed values (the bill amount and reservedAmount), not a projection and not a plan. WHAT IT MUST NOT DO, and these are the whole risk: (1) it must never read as a shortfall when EARLY FUNDING = 0 and the bill is simply not funded yet -- the marker is 'amount exceeds the reserve at its due date', not 'nothing reserved'; (2) it must never imply the reserve can be tapped or topped up from elsewhere, because it cannot; (3) it must never propose or trigger a transfer to cover the gap -- any reallocation is a proposal that goes through propose -> approve -> execute -> readback, and the display must not be a side effect that moves money; (4) it must not present the gap as a forecast of what WILL happen, only as the difference between what the bill is and what is set aside now; (5) it must not judge the owner's pocket allocation, which they have deliberately set low while tight. The unused 663.27-vs-1442 Rent case is the live fixture, and the honest sentence is the point: Rent needs 1442.00, 1097.10 is set aside, 344.90 has to come from spendable cash. OWNER CONFIRMED THE ARRANGEMENT 2026-09-20, so the design is now settled rather than proposed: Rent was due 2026-09-19 and WAS short; the gap STAYS OPEN and is resolved automatically when Rent is paid, with the shortfall taken out of spendable funds so Free to Spend falls by the gap. Therefore (6) NOTHING is re-targeted at the gap -- no future funding is aimed at closing it, and 'the reserve is short' is a fact to state, never a condition to repair; (7) the display names WHERE the shortfall comes from (spendable funds) rather than only its size, because that is the owner's actual arrangement; and (8) REAL-WORLD LATENESS IS NOT MODELLED -- the owner's instruction is that Meridian and Crew do not need to know that a payment is late in real life, so there is no deferred-obligation concept, no lateness flag and no owner-intent annotation for this case. The next Rent occurrence is funded normally by Crew's own proration (663.27 per biweekly event against a 1442.00 bill), which needs no special case. OWNER CONDITION 2026-09-20, which governs whether this ships at all: 'I dont know that it is necessary. But if its something you can do, and the visual display of it is easy to understand and informative, then absolutely.' So this is CONDITIONALLY approved, not mandated: it ships only if the display is EASY TO UNDERSTAND and INFORMATIVE. A design that needs explanation, reads as a warning, nags, or implies the reserve can be topped up has failed the condition even if its arithmetic is right. tasks.title: Draft owner-requested bill restructuring -- new bills, one-time modifications, and restoring the ongoing bill -- applied only with approval (propose-only)
tasks.detail: OWNER-RAISED 2026-09-20, AUTHORITY ALREADY DECIDED: propose-only. WHAT THE WORK ACTUALLY IS -- corrected after the owner explained the cause. My first framing implied a defect to repair ('one-time entries that should recur'). The owner corrected it: these entries are DELIBERATE WORKAROUNDS. Crew has NO option for a bill with only one due date, so when a budget is exceeded and he negotiates a payment arrangement with a biller (his examples: Verizon 75.00 due the 22nd monthly, Eversource 210.00 due the 30th), he must either create a NEW bill for the negotiated amount on the new date, or modify the existing bill ONE TIME -- and he usually also redoes the original bill so the following month starts on the correct date. In his words: 'These arent things crew or meridian have to worry about, the underlying budget system still works the same, its me tinkering with it because budgets were exceeded and I needed to find a workaround.' So the capability is to make HIS OWN requested restructuring FAST and EXACT, not to detect and correct anything. THE SLICE: Meridian can draft a precise bill change -- create a new bill, one-time-modify an existing bill, or restore the ongoing bill to its normal amount and date -- naming the bill, the current observed value, the proposed value, the reason, and the evidence, and routing it through the EXISTING propose -> approve -> execute -> readback engine (R30 already wired update_bill, update_bill_reserve_settings and create_autopilot_rule; do NOT build a second engine). The owner approves each one individually. WHAT IT MUST DO: state the exact field and both values so approval is a decision and not a guess; show the provider's current value as observed, with freshness, rather than trusting local state; and carry the outcome honestly through execution and provider verification, including refusal and unresolved receipts. WHAT IT MUST NOT DO: (1) never apply a change without an explicit owner approval of that specific change -- no 'confidence high enough to act', no batching into one silent sweep, no preapproved-automation class (explicitly not authorized); (2) never invent an intended schedule -- if the owner has to state it, record it as owner-supplied; (3) never widen the authority of any cheap classifier: per the OS-056 rule a classifier may only ADD friction, never remove an approval; (4) each proposal changes ONE thing the owner asked to change and says so plainly: a date correction never silently alters the amount, and an amount change is never smuggled in as a consequence of a recurrence fix -- BOTH are in scope as separate, explicitly-stated changes (the owner is adjusting Verizon and Eversource dates AND amounts right now), and what stays forbidden is a change the owner did not ask for riding along with one he did; (5) NEVER treat a one-time entry as an error -- it is the owner's workaround for a Crew limitation, so there is no detection, no nagging, and no 'should recur' proposal unless the owner asks for one; and (6) no payment-arrangement feature, no one-time-bill semantics, and no lifecycle tracking of 'modified for one cycle' -- those are explicit non-goals in the roadmap, because the underlying budget mechanics are unchanged. DEPENDENCY WORTH CHECKING FIRST: OS-053 (the candidate-to-commitment mapping exists twice and disagrees) is adjacent and should be settled or explicitly ruled out before bill identity is used to draft changes.

tasks.title: Fix the flaky credential-tampering test that carried an unexplained 1-in-256 failure
tasks.detail: FOUND AND FIXED 2026-09-20 while running the non-browser suite for an unrelated docs-only slice, which is how it surfaced: `tests/crew/test_session_credentials.py::test_cipher_rejects_tampering_and_wrong_key` failed once, then passed 5/5 in isolation, which is the signature of a nondeterministic defect rather than a real regression. ROOT CAUSE, proven by reproduction rather than reasoned about: the test built its tampered value as `encrypted.ciphertext[:-1] + b"x"`, which OVERWRITES the final byte instead of changing it. Whenever the ciphertext already ended in 0x78 -- the byte for 'x' -- the 'tampered' value was BYTE-IDENTICAL to the original, decryption correctly succeeded, and `pytest.raises(CredentialDecryptionError)` failed. A short reproduction found such a ciphertext on attempt 14 and printed 'old tamper is byte-identical to the original: True' and 'decrypt(tampered) -> NO ERROR', so the mechanism is demonstrated, not inferred. Frequency: the last byte must be 0x78, so roughly one run in 256 -- rare enough to look like noise, and it is a SECURITY test, where a spurious failure teaches people to ignore failures. FIX: flip the final byte with XOR (`bytes([encrypted.ciphertext[-1] ^ 0x01])`) so the tamper always changes something, plus an explicit `assert tampered_bytes != encrypted.ciphertext` guard so the test can never silently become a no-op again. VERIFIED: the same flip logic ran over 5000 fresh encryptions with ZERO failures to detect, the test passes 8/8 consecutive runs, the file is Ruff-clean, and the full non-browser suite is green at 1417 passed / 1 skipped. NOTE FOR TRIAGE HABITS: this is why 'a test failed but it passes on re-run' should be diagnosed rather than re-run until green -- the re-run was hiding a 0.4% false-alarm rate in a security assertion.

tasks.title: Constraint-driven adjustment planning: from an unforeseen cost to one validated plan of bill/pocket/autopilot proposals
tasks.detail: THE OWNER'S ORIGINAL MOTIVATION FOR MERIDIAN'S AI FEATURES, stated 2026-09-20 in his own words: 'the ability to say something like, I had to pay 500 dollars to repair my car, I cant cover this bill, look at the foreseeable future and make any budget/bill/autopilot adjustments necessary (proposals are then generated). I may add a stipulation like, I need at least 600 dollars free to spend each pay period, so meridian would make sure my pocket rule is for 600 dollars to free to spend.' THIS RECORDS THE TARGET; IT DOES NOT AUTHORISE BUILDING IT NOW. STATUS: open, deliberately unstarted, because its prerequisites are real and unmet. THE CAPABILITY, in three parts. (1) INPUT: an unforeseen cost plus a goal -- 'I paid 500 for the car', 'I cannot cover this bill'. (2) OWNER STIPULATIONS: standing constraints the plan must satisfy, e.g. a minimum free-to-spend per pay period, which would set the pocket rule to that amount. These are OWNER-SET POLICY held in Meridian (Crew has no equivalent field) and they BOUND THE PROPOSAL SPACE -- they are not a classifier output, they cannot remove an approval, and per the OS-056 rule nothing may ever turn a score into a path around owner approval. A stipulation that cannot be satisfied must produce a refusal or a plan that names what it cannot meet, never a silently weakened constraint. (3) OUTPUT: PROPOSALS across budget, bill and autopilot settings -- the 'one validated plan for the executor' already specified in roadmap I.3, never a debate transcript, never applied automatically. Every change carries its evidence, what it assumes, and what would change the answer; each is approved, executed and verified against the provider by readback. PREREQUISITES, in order, all recorded elsewhere: roadmap I.1 (envelope AND permissions; no role ever gets a provider write tool), I.2 (one role proven end to end, read-only and evidence-bound), I.3 (council producing one validated plan); Track C V2 (plan a paycheck without counting the same cash twice) and V3 (finish an authorised intervention and get an honest receipt); OS-059 (the connector readback gaps -- the sweep threshold and the pocket-allocation setting -- without which the pocket rule cannot be read, let alone reasoned about); and the existing propose -> approve -> execute -> readback engine, which is NOT to be rebuilt. WHAT IT MUST NOT DO: (1) never mutate anything -- it emits proposals; (2) never invent an owner stipulation, and never reinterpret one to a different number; (3) never present a plan as fact, a forecast as a balance, or a simulation as real money (D-013/D-015); (4) never assume the bill set or a due date is stable, since dates can move without the owner (Rent went 5th to 16th to 18th, the last not by him) and the bill set may change shape and revert; (5) never flag a payment-arrangement bill or a one-time bill as an error -- they are the owner's workarounds; (6) never model real-world lateness; (7) fail closed when the foreseeable future is underdetermined rather than filling the gap with a plausible number. FIRST ARTIFACT WHEN IT IS REACHED (framing corrected after the owner's design constraint): the OWNER STIPULATION store is a PRECONDITION, not the capability. It must exist as machine-readable owner policy so that a planner has a constraint to satisfy, and the read-only satisfaction checker is a useful deterministic TOOL. But per the owner's rule recorded in roadmap Track I -- 'An intelligence is needed because it shouldnt be prescribed to a preordained set of variables, virgil decides what needs to be done based on my input and proposes action' -- the DECISION of what needs doing is formed by an INTELLIGENCE reasoning over the actual situation, NEVER by a preordained variable set, a hardcoded decision table, or a lookup that maps a detected condition to a canned response. A design that can only act on anticipated cases has FAILED this task even if every test passes. Deterministic parts are TOOLS and CHECKS (arithmetic, stipulation satisfaction, freshness, provenance, readback verification): they make the output auditable and must never stand in for the decision itself. The review test is: could it handle a situation nobody wrote down? THE UNIFYING FRAME (owner, 2026-09-20): 'Thats the whole point of shortfall, virgils brief, proposals, automation. Its why almost full feature parity was so important. This was the whole point and vision all along.' So shortfall detection, Virgil's brief, the proposal engine and automation are ONE arc, not four features: detect a shortfall honestly -> analyse the foreseeable future -> generate proposals across every adjustable setting while honouring stipulations -> owner approves -> execute -> verify against the provider -> automate only what was explicitly preapproved. TWO CONSEQUENCES THAT CHANGE ORDERING: (a) FEATURE PARITY IS A PREREQUISITE, NOT POLISH -- Meridian must be able to READ AND ADJUST everything the owner can adjust in Crew (bills, reserves, pockets, autopilot rules, funding settings), because an adjustment it cannot read is one it cannot propose; this is why OS-059 sits ON this critical path rather than beside it. (b) VIRGIL IS THE FRONT DOOR to this arc, not a separate project: 'I should be able to ask virgil to analyze my financial situation and generate proposals to make all the in app adjustments I need to see me through, with any stipulations included' -- so VIRGIL-A1/A3 are the interface to OS-063, and A3's negative test (speech or model output can never select direct mutation provenance) is the safety property the whole arc rests on. NOTE ON INCOME TIMING, learned the hard way the same day: a paycheck's arrival day is a SEPARATE fact from a bill due date (the owner switched direct deposit to Crew, which has no early direct deposit, so income lands later while Rent stayed on the 16th) -- funding-event timing follows income arrival, never the due date, and Meridian must state what it OBSERVED rather than assert who caused a change. THE PROACTIVE HALF (owner, 2026-09-20), which is Track C V4 carrying this task's payload: 'I noticed you had to spend an extra 500 on ____, I propose to do these things to stay solvent without being cash starved in the meantime, and then return to steady state on this date, with your approval, I'll take care of all of it.' Four requirements the reactive form does not have: (1) MERIDIAN NOTICES -- the trigger is an OBSERVED deviation, not a request; (2) SOLVENCY AND LIQUIDITY ARE BOTH GOALS -- 'without being cash starved in the meantime' makes the liquidity floor INTEGRAL, so a plan that rebuilds the reserve by starving spendable cash is not a solution but the failure it was meant to prevent; (3) THE PLAN NAMES A RECOVERY DATE -- a plan with no end date is not a plan; (4) APPROVAL THEN EXECUTION -- one approval authorises the whole plan, Meridian executes it and the receipt is honest, with no part of the plan exempt from the gate. PREREQUISITES ADDED: V4's suppression/dedupe/feedback lifecycle is a PREREQUISITE, not a detail, because proactivity is where alert storms become the live risk -- note meridian/proactive.py is already wired but its lifecycle is UNVERIFIED in docs/project/CONCEPT_COVERAGE.md; the detection side must obey the OS-056 rule (a classifier may only ADD friction); and the natural front door for the proactive offer is VIRGIL-A4, gated by the addendum on C-V4 plus one proven I.2 role.

tasks.title: Read-only inbound bill-notice ingestion (email/statement) as planning evidence — trust boundary only, not yet authorised to build
tasks.detail: OWNER-DESCRIBED TRIGGER CLASS (2026-09-20), recorded so the ORDER is not lost: 'Or, I saw your bill increased by 40 dollars in your email, heres what needs to be adjusted with your approval -- I approve, and all adjustments occur etc.' So proactive triggers are PLURAL: an observed transaction deviation (OS-063) and an INBOUND NOTIFICATION read from the owner's inbox. Same shape -- notice -> 'here is what needs adjusting' -> one approval -> all adjustments occur. THIS TASK RECORDS THE TRUST BOUNDARY FIRST; IT DOES NOT AUTHORISE BUILDING. STATUS: open, unstarted, and it must not begin before the arc's prerequisites (OS-063, Track I.1/I.2, V4's suppression lifecycle) and before a security review of exactly how the mailbox is reached. REQUIRED PROPERTIES, none optional: (1) READ-ONLY AND LEAST PRIVILEGE -- Meridian reads notifications; it never sends, deletes, labels or mutates the mailbox, and it requests the narrowest scope that can read the relevant senders; (2) NO CREDENTIAL EXPOSURE EVER -- no OAuth token, refresh token, cookie, OTP, API key or message body is logged, echoed into stored evidence, included in a proposal, or handed to a model as instruction; the mailbox credential lives where the existing credential store lives and is never surfaced (this is a standing project rule, repeated here because a new data source is where it gets violated); (3) EMAIL CONTENT IS EVIDENCE, NEVER INSTRUCTIONS -- a notification is untrusted input that can be wrong AND hostile, so it can never direct tool use, never select an action, and never be treated as authorization; this is the same rule already applied to web search results, and it is the prompt-injection boundary for this feature; (4) VERIFY AGAINST THE BILL OF RECORD -- 'your bill increased by 40 dollars' is a CLAIM; Crew's readback is the AUTHORITY, and the proposal must show the observed provider value beside the claim, with the email demoted to the reason the check happened; (5) SUPPRESSION IS A PRECONDITION -- one message per bill per cycle is not an alert stream, and re-reading the same message must never re-propose the same change, so V4's dedupe/lifecycle (currently UNVERIFIED for meridian/proactive.py per CONCEPT_COVERAGE.md) must be settled first; (6) NO MUTATION OF ANY KIND IN THIS SLICE -- it produces evidence and candidate changes for OS-063's proposal path, and approval through the existing engine remains the only route to a provider write. FAIL-CLOSED: if the sender is unrecognised, the amount cannot be parsed with confidence, or the claim disagrees with Crew's readback, the outcome is 'could not confirm' rather than a proposal.
